title: Backfill-and-Fallback-Runbook-Dry-Run
content:
Summary:

This doc captures the dry-run we ran on 2027-11-17 to validate the backfill and fallback sections of the SRE runbook for inference service degradations. The session covered: synthetic traffic backfills to simulate missed requests during an outage, verification of automated fallback to cheaper model variants, and exercising the manual backfill play when auto-backfill is disabled.

Why we ran this:
- Recent incidents (see SRE-4123) showed gaps in the backfill path: delayed KV-cache warmup and duplicate-cost risk when replaying requests.
- We needed to ensure the fallback pipeline (route -> model-variant -> throttling) behaves with real-world prefix cache states.

Attendees:
- On-call: Arjun Patel (primary), Leah Rivera (secondary)
- Observers/engineers: Maya Chen (facilitator), Tomás Ortega (runtime), Riley Park (monitoring)

Preconditions and setup:
- Environment: staging-inference-v2, region us-west-2 (matches production configs for routing and cache TTLs).
- Feature flags: auto-backfill enabled (toggle: infra.auto_backfill = true) for run 1, disabled for run 2.
- Mock workload: 50k synthetic requests over 10m representing mix: 60% short-chat (seq<64), 30% long-completion (seq>512), 10% embeddings.
- Baseline metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latency, request error rate, model-invocation count, KV cache hit ratio, token cost estimate.

Dry-run timeline (high level):
- 09:00 start: baseline snapshot taken (see linked Grafana panel: SLO -> inference / staging).
- 09:05 simulated control-plane failure (circuit) for 45s to simulate lost in-flight token-index writes (this creates a backfill window).
- 09:06-09:16 synthetic traffic injected at 5x baseline.
- 09:17 validated auto-backfill behavior (run 1).
- 09:40 repeated with auto-backfill disabled to test manual procedure (run 2).
- 10:15 debrief and log collection.

Observations (auto-backfill enabled):
- Auto-backfill started a replay worker within ~14s after control-plane restoration. Expected target <= 10s. Reason: leader election delay + small bug in queue-check backoff. (See PR candidate: infra#1745.)
- KV cache warmup lagged for long-completion paths; p95 token generation spiked by ~1.8x for sequences >512 during the first 30s of replay. Cache hit ratio recovered after ~80s.
- Model fallback routing (to smaller quantized variant q4b) triggered correctly when dedicated capacity was saturated, but fallback path did not propagate original request metadata (trace ids) — causes gap in tracing.
- Cost accounting: naive replays produced ~1.25x estimated token cost in first minute due to concurrent retries. We observed duplicate replays for ~1% of keys (race in lease-check).

Observations (manual backfill, auto-backfill disabled):
- Manual procedure (runbook step: trigger-backfill.sh followed by monitor-check) worked end-to-end, but operator needed to wait for health-check green before scaling replay workers to avoid backend saturation.
- There was some ambiguity in the runbook about when to re-enable autoscaling (step 4 vs step 6); operators re-enabled too early which caused thrash.
- Handoff notes: on-call documented the window and created SRE-4124 for followups.

SLO/alerts impact during runs:
- Request latency SLO (p95 < 1200ms) breached for ~95s total during run 1 (spike concentrated first 30s).
- Error budget: simulated breach only in staging counters, but replay cost burn rate would have consumed ~3% of a monthly budget if run in prod at scale.

Runbook issues found (concrete):
- Missing step: ensure trace_id propagation when fallback to model-variant occurs. Add explicit header pass-through clause.
- Backoff bug: replay-worker queue-check uses exponential backoff with a max of 30s; reduce to 8s for faster recovery in typical leader-election scenarios.
- Duplicate replay race: add optimistic lease owner write + compare-and-set (CAS) to prevent two workers replaying same key.
- Autoscale guidance ambiguous: define clear metrics (queue length per worker > X) and minimum cooldown (120s) before scaling further.

Handoff / On-call notes for next shift:
- Primary on-call: Arjun Patel -> leave note with links to logs in S3: s3://redwood-ops/backfill-runs/2027-11-17/ and the consolidated runbook transcript.
- If similar real incident occurs: 1) toggle infra.auto_backfill=false to avoid duplicate risk, 2) run manual-backfill with 1 worker/10k backlog and monitor queue-length metric (infra.backfill.queue.len) until steady, 3) escalate to runtime team if KV hit ratio remains < 40% after 120s.
- Slack shorthand created: #sre-backfill-run (thread TS: C09ABCD8E-1634) — link in linked_artifacts.

Action items and owners (short):
- infra: reduce replay backoff and add CAS lease (owner: Tomás) — target: 2027-11-24 — linked to PR infra#1745.
- runtime: ensure trace_id and request metadata preserved during model-variant fallback (owner: Leah) — target: 2027-11-22.
- runbooks: update manual-backfill section with explicit autoscale cooldown and add checklist for pre-warm KV (owner: Maya) — target: 2027-11-19.
- monitoring: add an alert to surface duplicate replay rate > 0.1% (owner: Riley) — target: 2027-11-21.

Unresolved questions / follow ups:
- Should auto-backfill have a soft-sample mode that replays at 10% rate first to warm cache before full replay? Pros: reduce cost spike; cons: longer total backfill time. Request product input.
- For trace continuity, do we accept eventual consistency in spans or require instantaneous continuity? Tradeoffs matter for audits.

Notes to reviewers:
- Logs and metric snapshots uploaded to the run artifact S3 path above.
- Repro steps are in infra/runbooks/backfill-dry-run.md (branch: staging-tests).
- Please review infra#1745 for the proposed fix; it addresses both backoff and duplicate replay race.

Appendix (quick metrics snapshot):
- Baseline p95 (staging): 420ms
- Peak p95 during first run window: 1180ms (breach)
- KV cache hit ratio baseline: 87% -> dipped to 24% immediate post-control-plane window -> recovered to 79% after 80s
- Estimated token cost multiplier first 60s: 1.25x

End notes: this felt like a high-value exercise — caught 3 medium-risk issues we should prioritize before enabling auto-backfill in new regions. Assigning follow-ups now. If you were on the run: add any missed observations below (edit in doc).
